data.content_ref: inline:The argument asserts that a single engine cannot escape its own 'latent manifold' because self-consistency bias keeps the probability distribution peaked, but it provides no causal mechanism establishing that separation of engines defeats that bias. Different engines trained on overlapping corpora can share the same systematic blind spot, so merely splitting authoring from checking across engines is not causally sufficient for independent verification. The mechanism also lacks a count/execute test: it invokes 'likely' failure to recognize an anomaly as an error but does not specify what to count or execute in a single run's record to distinguish a real audit from peak-traversal. Its own counterconditions (temperature, persona shifts) concede alternative causal routes, undermining the claim of necessity.
